bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge RTL, spi_passthrough always generates the downstream SPI clock by clock-gating host_sck_i directly. The module had no knowledge of the configured SPI clock polarity and no inverted host clock input. For CPOL=1 (SPI mode 3), the host SCK idles high, so the filter/gating sequence that was designed for an idle-low clock re-enables the downstream clock at the wrong point. As a result, after a filtered command the downstream device misses or mis-times the first clock edge of the next transaction, breaking passthrough operation in CPOL=1. The fix must propagate the CPOL configuration and an inverted host SCK into spi_passthrough, gate both clock polarities, and select the correct gated clock for the downstream SCK output based on CPOL.
bug_info.fix_hint: Add cfg_cpol_i and host_isck_i ports to spi_passthrough and connect them from spi_device. Gate both host_sck_i and host_isck_i with the existing sck_gate_en, using separate clock-gating cells. Then drive passthrough_o.sck from the normal gated clock when CPOL is 0 and from the inverted gated clock when CPOL is 1, so that the downstream clock polarity and the filter/enable timing are consistent with the SPI mode.
